title: Through the waters (Isaiah 43:2)
hookLine: "When thou passest through the waters, I will be with thee"

lines: I HAVE CALLED THEE BY THY NAME.
cards: "Fear not." Two words, early in Isaiah forty-three, and then a run of reasons, said to a people far from home: "I have redeemed thee, I have called thee by thy name; thou art mine." Not a crowd.
A name. The very next verse turns to water and fire, and in the King James it doesn't say if. It says when.
When the water is up to your chest. When the river is moving faster than you are. When the fire is close enough to feel.

teach.h: NO PROMISE OF A DRY ROAD.
teach.b: Verse two: "When thou passest through the waters, I will be with thee; and through the rivers, they shall not overflow thee: when thou walkest through the fire, thou shalt not be burned."

teach.h: A PROMISE OF COMPANY, AND A LIMIT.
teach.b: Read it slowly, and notice what it doesn't promise. No promise that there will be no waters. No bridge, no detour, no dry season.
It promises company: I will be with thee. And it promises a limit: the rivers shall not overflow thee. The water comes up.
It doesn't close over your head. Look at the verbs, too. Passest through.
Walkest through. The person in this verse keeps moving. Nobody is told to stand still in the river or camp in the fire.
Through means there is another side. Some readers hear the people's own story here. A sea split open when they left Egypt.
A river held back when they crossed into the land.

teach.h: THEY HAD WALKED THROUGH WATER BEFORE.
teach.b: Isaiah's listeners, far from home, are reminded that they have walked through water before. The verse doesn't explain why the hard thing comes, or say the fire is a lesson. It simply stands in the water beside them.
In the chapter, that's the whole of the comfort: you are named, you are not alone in it, and it will not cover you.

how: Jews read Isaiah 43 among the prophets' words of comfort to the exiles, and its promise of God's presence in hard times is a verse some turn to in illness, grief and danger.

o: the leader who brought the people across the sea
the prophet swallowed by a fish on his way to sea
the prophet who promised company through deep water

games.q: through the waters — tap the pairs.

s: the verse promises you'll never face deep water
it says when thou passest through the waters, not if.
the verse's promise is company: I will be with thee
and a limit: the rivers shall not overflow thee.
the verse explains why the hard thing comes
it gives no reason. it promises presence and another side.

games.q: you're in the river, and it's rising. what does the verse promise?
o: I will be with thee, and it won't overflow thee.
games.why: "when thou passest through the waters, I will be with thee." company, and a limit, not a dry road.

practice: Name the water you're in right now, the thing that feels deeper than you'd like, and don't try to drain it; just notice where it reaches, your ankles, your chest, and whether your head is still above it. Breathe there for a while.
If you pray, you can hold the verse: I will be with thee.

wordCard.voice: Isaiah, who promised a people far from home that passing through deep water or fire would come with company, and with a limit: it would not close over them.

orig.note: Hebrew: when you pass through the waters, from Isaiah 43:2.

carryVoice: Your line: the waters won't overflow. Not if, but when, and not alone. Day seven hundred ninety, done.
